user.text:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
The book tracker is built, and the tests, the production build and a check against the running server all pass. Books are saved to data/books.json and are still there after a restart.

To run it: npm run dev, then open http://localhost:3000. For a production run, use npm run build && npm start.

- Home page: shows "Currently reading" (newest first) with a "Mark finished" button on each book, and "Finished" with the date each was finished. The add-book form is at the bottom: title is required, author and notes are optional.
- Book page: clicking a title opens /books/<id> with the title, author, status and your notes. That address is the link you can send someone, and the browser tab shows "Title by Author". An unknown link gets a "Book not found" page.
- Saving: the file is created the first time you add a book. Each save writes a new file and swaps it in, so a crash mid-save can't corrupt it. Saves also run one at a time, so two quick adds can't overwrite each other. data/ is in .gitignore so your list stays out of git.

What I ran:
- npm test: 6 tests pass, covering adding, saving, marking finished, a missing title, unknown books and 20 books added at once.
- npm run build: succeeds.
- With some sample books loaded into the running server:
  - The home page and a book page showed the right content.
  - Notes containing HTML were displayed as text, not run as HTML.
  - A made-up book link returned 404.
  - "Mark finished" worked; I sent the form directly, as a browser without JavaScript would.
  - After a restart the book was still marked finished.

I didn't send the add-book form through the running server. That form is covered only by the tests of the saving code, so it's worth one quick manual try.

Anyone who can open the site can add or finish books. That's fine on your own machine. But the other person can only open a link you send if the app runs somewhere they can reach. If you put it online, it needs at least a password first. Also, many hosting platforms wipe local files, so the JSON file only works on a server with persistent disk.

The code is in app/ (the pages and form handling) and lib/books.js (reading and writing the JSON file). I added Next.js 16 and React 19 to package.json and set up the dev, build, start and test scripts. Nothing is committed.
